summary_for_children: Al-Anbiya means The Prophets. It reminds us that the heavens and the earth were made by Allah, and tells briefly of many prophets: Ibrahim and the fire, Dawud and Sulayman, Ayyub, Yunus, Zakariyya and others, who all called to worship Allah alone.
environment_concept: Rooms of signs: a spring (21:30), an empty ring of stones where the fire was made cool (21:69; no fire or person is shown), mountains with birds (21:79), a sail full of wind (21:81) and a dark sea at night (21:87).
architecture_and_scenery: Colonnade of plain stone rooms, each with a single symbolic object: a cooled fire pit, mountains and birds, a wind-driven sail, a whale-dark sea.

palette.lighting: Shifting daylight with a slow-orbiting sun and moon above the gallery

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A quiet courtyard with three lecterns holding prayer tablets and three carved doors in an arc

primary_mechanic.text: Three lecterns hold the prayers of Ayyub, Yunus and Zakariyya as verified verses; three doors each tell of a situation. Read a prayer, carry it, and set it in the door it answers; that door opens on the verse telling how it was answered. The wrong door refuses it.

secondary_activities: Ibrahim and the statues (21:51-56, 21:69, read only)
unique_world.narrative_structure: The three prayers and doors, then the Ibrahim sign, then the palms
world_assets: three carved doors with signs (bent stem, dark waves, lamp)
environment_behaviour: doors swing open and light spills through when answered
the status line shows a door's situation when you stand by it
unique_world.learning_objective: Learn three prayers of the prophets in the Quran and that they were answered (21:83-90)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Prophets' Legacy
story_library.children_narration: Allah sent many prophets to guide people. Ibrahim challenged the worship of idols and was saved from the fire. Ayyub called upon Allah during suffering, Yunus prayed in distress, and Zakariyya prayed for a child. Their stories show different forms of patience, courage, and faith.

world_idea.title: The Hall of Prophetic Journeys
world_idea.description: Explore separate environments for Ibrahim, Ayyub, Yunus, and Zakariyya. Each has a different exploration mechanic: reasoning, patience, supplication, or discovering the story through its setting.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: Ibrahim in the fire (21:68-70) is reading only, with no fire scene with a person.
